description: Wait budgets for the Meta_Kim Live singleton hub. A freshly spawned hub child indexes every governed run artifact before it publishes its state, so its ready time is a property of the project and the machine rather than a constant the launcher can carry. On a 256-run project three consecutive fresh starts took 2175ms, 2368ms and 4175ms, and an already-published hub is re-verified in 2-3ms. An earlier series on the same project read 5889ms to 15574ms, but those samples timed the launcher rather than the child: every 75ms poll then ran a Windows process creation-time query costing 1867-5020ms, so a hub that was ready at two seconds went unnoticed for several more and the 5000ms budget in force at the time reported startup_timeout. A dead child is detected from its exit code rather than from this budget, so a generous ceiling costs nothing when startup genuinely fails.

budgetNotes.startupBudgetMs: The user asked for the hub directly, so waiting is what they want. Bounded only so a hung child still reports a failure.
budgetNotes.hookAutostartBudgetMs: Live is an optional observation surface started alongside a governed run, so this fuse is short enough not to hold the run hostage. It is paid at most once per session: an already-running hub is reused in 2-3ms. It keeps close to a threefold margin over the slowest measured 4175ms start, because a false startup_timeout costs the feature while a wedged child costs this wait once.
budgetNotes.stopBudgetMs: Waits for a process to exit rather than for it to index, so it does not need the startup budget.
